169: Takings claim: HUD's abatement of HAP payments and withholding of approval for sale was not a regulatory taking under the Penn Central factors.
The Claims Court correctly determined that the Penn Central factors do not support Normandy's takings claim.
275: Regulatory takings: dismissal of the regulatory takings claim based on the golden parachute prohibition, which left intact the contract breach remedy against Freddie Mac.
We affirm the Claims Court's dismissal of Mr. Piszel's regulatory takings claim.
276: Per se or categorical takings (physical and total-deprivation categories): no categorical taking found and the claims were dismissed.
the government's actions did not amount to a total taking of Mr. Piszel's property because the government's actions left intact his potential breach of contract claim against Freddie Mac.
766: Whether the Forest Service's installation of bat gates on two mine claims constituted a compensable taking under the Fifth Amendment (permanent physical occupation or denial of meaningful access); court found no taking and affirmed summary judgment for the government.

Because there is no genuine issue of material fact regarding whether the bat gates constitute a permanent physical occupation or deny claimants meaningful access to the mines for the purposes of conducting the limited, permissible activities, the Court of Federal Claims did not err in ruling that the government was entitled to summary judgment.
867: Takings: Straw failed to plead a compensable taking under the Fifth Amendment; the bodily-integrity claim sounds in tort, not property.
Accordingly, Mr. Straw failed to plead a takings claim under the Fifth Amendment.
1019: Takings claim based on alleged conduct by military members failed because the officers' acts were not shown to be authorized by federal law, so no taking was stated
Her allegations therefore cannot support a takings claim.
1028: Takings claim based on frustration of a legal claim by district court dismissal was not a compensable taking.
We have held that frustration of a legal claim, like that alleged by Plaintiffs, is not a compensable taking.
1253: Regulatory takings: whether FDA press releases and a media briefing warning of a salmonella link to tomatoes constituted government action effecting a regulatory taking; court held no taking was alleged.
In the instant case, because the Tomato Producers have failed to raise a regulatory takings claim, we affirm the dismissal of the Claims Court.
1284: Takings: whether conversion of the elevated viaduct into the High Line Park under the National Trails System Act was a taking of Romanoff's property. The court held that the 1932 easement was broad enough to cover trail and park use, so Romanoff held no property interest taken by the United States.

Accordingly the trial court properly held that Romanoff did not at any time acquire a property interest in the viaduct easement that was taken by the United States and for which Romanoff is entitled to compensation.
1421: Physical taking of water rights via alleged government harassment and threats of prosecution at 1866 Act ditches; court held no physical taking because the government merely restricted use rather than occupying the property, and no further remand proceedings on that theory.
Where, as here, the government merely restricts the use of an individual's property—instead of occupying that property—that individual has not suffered a physical taking.
1482: Regulatory takings: whether BLM's 1995 MOU effected a compensable temporary taking under Penn Central; court held no compensable taking.
we agree with the Claims Court's judgment that the Government's acts did not effect a compensable taking of Reoforce's property.
1594: Takings: Starr's alternative Fifth Amendment taking and unconstitutional conditions theories for the equity acquisition, not reached on the merits

Accordingly, we have no occasion in this case to address whether the Government's acquisition of AIG equity was an illegal exaction; what damages, if any, would attach; and whether the unconstitutional conditions doctrine has any applicability in this case.
1634: Whether the STB-issued NITU and conversion of the former railroad corridor into a recreational trail under the Trails Act effected a compensable taking; the court held the landowners retained no property interest because the deeds conveyed fee simple title to the railroad.
the language of the six deeds-at-issue clearly convey fee simple title to Seaboard on their face.
2442: Takings: the claim that the unpaid penalty amounts were a taking failed because Lagergren has no property interest in a statutory right to be paid money.
Lagergren must first show that he has a property interest in the delayed amounts owed, which he has not and cannot do here.
2459: Takings claim based on termination of employment fails because no valid property interest was alleged.
the Court of Federal Claims did not err in dismissing Hood's takings claim for failure to state a claim upon which relief may be granted.
2674: Trade secrets takings claim dismissed: taking by a private party cannot be a Government taking; affirmed
In addition, he cannot sue the Government for an alleged taking by a private party.
3013: Takings: whether a Fifth Amendment taking occurred where Walker's comments were not authorized government action; dismissal for failure to state a takings claim affirmed
Because no authorized government action was implicated, the Claims Court correctly dismissed Dr. Filler's takings claim for failure to state a claim under RCFC 12(b)(6).
3242: Count III: whether the Claims Resolution Act of 2010 effected a taking of Counts I and II; court held no taking occurred because appellants chose not to opt out
We conclude that no taking occurred here.
3353: Regulatory taking under Lucas: whether the government's permit denial eliminated all economic value of Plat 57, so that the residual noneconomic (environmental) value does not preclude a per se Lucas taking.
We affirm the trial court's holding that the government's permit denial constituted a per se regulatory taking under Lucas because Plat 57's residual value is not attributable to any economic uses.
3678: Takings claim: the transmission of plaintiff's thoughts did not involve private property within the Takings Clause, so no plausible taking was alleged
We therefore agree with the court that Mr. Harris has not plausibly alleged a taking.
3728: Fifth Amendment takings: whether the imposition of taxes and liens constitutes a taking; held not a taking.
Nor do we see any error in the Claims Court's holding that "an imposition of taxes is not a taking for Fifth Amendment purposes."
3772: Takings: whether the government's requiring or approving the levee on Givens' farm constituted a Fifth Amendment taking of the Welty Farm; claim dismissed for failure to plead government responsibility (no agency, no coercion, no direct and intended result).
The Landowners have pled no facts suggesting that the alleged flooding of their farm was a direct and intended result of the government's actions with respect to Givens.
3819: Fifth Amendment takings claim based on the reduced statutory dividend rate, under both the statutory-entitlement theory and the alternative capital-investment theory; no compensable taking found.
Because the complaint fails to allege facts sufficient to support a taking under the Fifth Amendment, the trial court properly dismissed this claim under RCFC 12(b)(6).
4181: Takings: whether Hardy holds a compensable property interest. The court held the MG&AR form deeds, the Lee deed, and the County Road 213 deeds conveyed easements, not fee simple estates, so Hardy has a compensable property interest.

Because we conclude that the MG&AR form deeds and the Lee deed granted easements to the Railroad, and that the County Road 213 deeds granted easements to the State Highway Department of Georgia, we hold that Hardy has a compensable property interest.
4182: Takings: whether issuance of the NITU effected a temporary physical taking of parcels east of milepost E-65.80. The court vacated and remanded for the trial court to decide whether and when the railroad would have abandoned absent the NITU under Caquelin, without reaching the merits.
we vacate and remand for the parties to address this issue before the trial court in the first instance.
4287: Takings claim accrual under the stabilization doctrine; claim held time-barred under 28 U.S.C. § 2501 because the permanent nature of the erosion was evident by 2006.
the Court of Federal Claims did not err when it found that the claim should not be suspended.
4330: Takings: Langan failed to identify a cognizable property interest taken by the United States under the Fifth Amendment; no taking found.
the Claims Court correctly concluded that Mr. Langan failed to identify a cognizable property interest that had been taken by the United States.
4404: Whether Treasury's denial of redemption was a taking of the States' property; court held no property interest was impaired, so no taking
Because no property interest of the States has been impaired, there can be no taking.
4458: Takings: whether GIP had a cognizable property interest in the slag the EPA recovered, so that a compensable taking of slag occurred; Federal Circuit reversed the trial court's finding and vacated the slag damages award.
GIP cannot establish a cognizable property interest in the slag that the EPA recovered.
4618: Takings: cancellation of patent claims in inter partes review is not a Fifth Amendment taking; failure to state a takings claim.
the cancellation of Christy's patent claims in an inter partes review was not a Fifth Amendment taking.
4641: Takings: the Federal Circuit affirmed that the Board's issuance of a NITU that blocked abandonment and continued the railroad easement is a categorical (temporary) taking under Ladd I, rejecting the government's request to apply the Penn Central or Arkansas Game multi-factor analysis.
We reject the contention that Arkansas Game calls for displacing the categorical-taking analysis adopted in our precedents for a NITU that blocks termination of an easement
4642: Takings timing and causation: the court clarified that no taking occurs for a NITU period if the railroad would have abandoned the line anyway during that period. It accepted the government's legal point but rejected its evidentiary-insufficiency argument, so the taking still stood for the NITU period.
We agree with the government's legal point but not its assertion of evidentiary insufficiency.
4855: Fifth Amendment takings claim based on termination of Appellants' lawsuits against Libya; no compensable taking under Penn Central factors (assuming a cognizable property interest).
we hold that even if Appellants had a property interest in their lawsuits, no taking occurred under the Fifth Amendment.
4941: Takings: Su Casa's Penn Central claim disposed of on summary judgment because the complete lack of reasonable investment-backed expectations (purchase after enactment of the Preservation Statutes) was dispositive; judgment affirmed.

We agree with the Claims Court that there is no genuine dispute regarding Su Casa's inability to prove that it purchased the property with an expectation that it would later be able to prepay the mortgage.
4942: Takings: economic impact prong for remaining FWPs; Claims Court erred in limiting economic impact measure to fair market value change and in rejecting Dr. Wade's lost-income, benchmarking, severity and ex post data analyses on summary judgment; judgment vacated and remanded.
Thus, the Claims Court's grant of summary judgment with respect to the remaining FWPs is vacated and remanded for further proceedings.
4987: Takings: whether the Bureau of Reclamation's 2001 temporary halt of Klamath Project water deliveries was a compensable taking, where appellants' water rights were held subordinate to the Tribes' senior federal reserved water rights.

We therefore see no error in the court's holding that the Bureau of Reclamation's action in temporarily halting deliveries of Klamath Project water in 2001 did not constitute a taking of appellants' property.
5242: Takings: claim that the §363 sale violated the statute is not a cognizable takings action; remedy lies in the bankruptcy appeal process.
we disagree that this is a cognizable takings action.
5345: Takings: whether the NITU/Trails Act conversion of the railroad right-of-way effected a taking of landowners' reversionary interests; court held trial court misapplied the centerline presumption, so landowners' ownership claim is not foreclosed on summary judgment and the summary judgment for government is reversed and remanded.
We conclude that the trial court misapplied the centerline presumption to the evidence. We reverse and remand.
5421: Regulatory taking claim based on Air Force informal advice to Wind Energy; court held Tucker Act jurisdiction exists but claim fails on the merits under Penn Central.
The Taylors' regulatory-taking claim nevertheless fails on the merits as a matter of law.
5423: Physical taking claim based on Air Force overflights; complaint insufficient to state a physical taking under Causby and Brown factors.
Therefore, the Taylors failed to state a claim for a physical taking.
5543: Physical takings liability: the Court of Federal Claims clearly erred in finding the shoreline sandy and fully mitigated, so Government-caused erosion remains irreversible and Banks must be compensated for it on remand.
The Court of Federal Claims’ adoption of Dr. Nairn’s finding of a sandy shoreline was clearly erroneous.
5688: Physical taking: whether the government's Beasley fax asserting ownership of the gun mount site, sent to a prospective purchaser, was a physical or per se regulatory taking. Court held it was not a taking and reversed the CFC.

We hold that the government's mere sharing of information about its claim of ownership to real property with a third party does not constitute a physical taking (or a per se regulatory taking) of that property.
5773: Takings: the court held the complaints alleged a physical taking of usufructuary rights rather than a regulatory taking and rejected the government's argument that a taking must be predicated on United States action; no finding that a taking occurred.
We hold that the Water Districts alleged a physical taking, not a regulatory taking.
5793: Regulatory taking of the Master Lease and sublease under Penn Central and Lucas; court held no regulatory taking because plaintiffs showed no economic injury caused by WARA.
We conclude that WARA did not constitute a regulatory or physical taking. We therefore reverse.
5794: Physical taking of the Lemmon Avenue Terminal based on WARA incorporating the Five-Party Agreement and requiring Dallas to demolish the gates; court held no physical taking.

We find, however, that WARA did not codify the Five-Party Agreement in its entirety and specifically did not codify the portions of the Agreement in which Dallas agreed to acquire and demolish plaintiffs' gates.
5927: Takings, contract-based theory: whether repudiation of the prepayment right effected a taking of a contract right; court held no taking because the Government did not substantially take away the right to damages.
Accordingly, Appellants cannot succeed on a takings theory premised on a breach of their prepayment right.
5928: Takings, property-based regulatory theory: whether ELIHPA and HCDA's restrictions on prepayment effected a compensable regulatory taking of Appellants' real property; court held the claim properly asserted and remanded for the Claims Court to decide compensability.

Having established that Appellants have presented a proper alternative takings claim based on the allegedly diminished value of their real property, the Claims Court must consider in the first instance whether such a claim is compensable.
6115: Takings claim from STB NITU conversion of railroad right-of-way to trail; court held the trial court misapplied Florida's centerline presumption in finding landowners did not own the corridor land, reversing summary judgment for the government and remanding.
We conclude that the trial court misapplied the centerline presumption to the evidence. We reverse and remand.
6152: Rails-to-trails taking: whether the Jones and Wilkins deeds conveyed fee simple or only an easement, so that claimants held no cognizable reversionary property interest and no compensable taking occurred from the STB's issuance of the NITU.

Appellants have failed to allege a cognizable property interest on which they can recover just compensation. For these reasons, the Government did not commit a compensable taking under the Fifth Amendment, and we affirm the final judgment of the trial court.
6171: Takings claim based on a statutory entitlement to full risk corridors payments; no property interest in a statutory obligation to pay money, so no taking.
We have previously held that "no statutory obligation to pay money, even where unchallenged, can create a property interest within the meaning of the Takings Clause."
6182: Fifth Amendment takings claim failed to state a claim because TGM irrevocably transferred the assets and waived claims to them, so no legally cognizable property interest existed.
We also agree with the Claims Court that Blodgett failed to state a Fifth Amendment takings claim upon which relief can be granted.
6257: Takings: whether the Government's espousal and settlement of appellants' claims against Libya and vacatur of their district court judgment was a compensable per se or regulatory taking; court held no compensable taking under Penn Central factors.
We hold that, even if Appellants have a property interest in their claims and non-final judgment, no compensable taking occurred under the Fifth Amendment.
6307: Whether cancellation of patent claims in a government-initiated inter partes review was a compensable taking: no taking found.
under Celgene, cancellation of patent claims in inter partes review cannot be a taking under the Fifth Amendment.
6308: Takings claims based on actions of the Claims Court and the Federal Circuit in the Lead Case: no taking.
the actions of the Federal Circuit and the Claims Court cannot be an unconstitutional taking, as both courts adjudicate rights in patents.
6460: Takings: the claim rests on alleged regulatory violations by the BIA, which cannot support a takings claim, so no cognizable taking was found.

The theory that the Moodys were harmed by the BIA's violation of regulations does not give rise to a takings claim but rather the right to appeal the lease cancellations through the administrative process at the BIA.
6481: Takings: the government-induced flooding of Eagle Lake; the court held the relative benefits doctrine forecloses liability, so no compensable taking.
We reverse the Claims Court's judgment because the relative benefits doctrine bars liability.
6516: Whether the twenty-six rail-corridor deeds conveyed fee simple title to the railroad (so no compensable Fifth Amendment taking) or only an easement; court held fee simple, so no taking.
we conclude that each of the twenty-six deeds conveyed fee simple title, not merely an easement, and we thus affirm the decision of the Court of Federal Claims.
6665: Takings: complaint does not allege a taking by the United States; alleged wrongful acts were by the Tribe, and a takings claim cannot rest on unlawful government action.
"[a] takings claim cannot be found on the theory that the United States has taken unlawful action."
6751: Takings claim based on state court judgments and New Jersey state actors; no taking found and no jurisdiction over state officials or state courts.
Jaye’s takings allegations all stem from what she believes are “void judgments made by state courts.”
6788: Taking of contractual prepayment rights: no compensable taking because contract interference gives rise to a breach claim, not a taking claim.
interference with such contractual rights generally gives rise to a breach claim not a taking claim.
7191: Takings claim failed: Shelden did not identify a valid property interest or plausibly allege a compensable taking, lacked standing to assert his son's property, and alleged an unauthorized executive taking; no takings jurisdiction.
Shelden has not made this showing.
7412: Takings liability based on government inaction: the court held that the government's failure to maintain or modify MRGO cannot support takings liability, which requires affirmative government acts.
Takings liability must be premised on affirmative government acts.
7413: Causation for the temporary flooding taking: the court held plaintiffs failed to prove that the construction or operation of MRGO caused their injury because they did not account for the risk-reducing LPV flood control levees.

Because plaintiffs failed to show that government action, including both MRGO and the LPV project, caused their injury, the government is not liable for a taking under the Fifth Amendment based on the construction or operation of MRGO.
7492: Takings: whether the amended complaint pleaded a cognizable property interest in the land taken for COP Millet under Afghan law, so as to state a Fifth Amendment taking claim.
Even accepting as true all factual allegations in Sharifi's amended complaint, the amended complaint does not contain sufficient facts to state a plausible takings claim.
7504: Takings: takings claim failed because the plaintiff did not plausibly plead a taking by the United States; any taking was by Alaska or its officials.

Accordingly, the Court of Federal Claims does not have jurisdiction over Mr. Sheakley's takings claim because any alleged taking was committed not by the United States, but instead by Alaska or its officials.
7616: Takings claim over escrowed Sberbank shares: no taking shown because the complaint did not concede validity of the government action, and in any event the national security freeze is not a compensable taking under Paradissiotis.
Thus, we conclude that Mr. Tindall's complaint does not 'concede the validity of the government action' and, absent concession, fails to state a claim.
7681: Takings: the court held that Mandry failed to allege a taking of private property for public use without compensation based on congressional inaction on Puerto Rico statehood and PROMESA.
Mr. Mandry has not alleged that the United States took his private property for public use without compensation.
8061: Cacciapalle's separate takings claim based on HERA's bar on derivative suits fails to state a claim
There is simply no claim embedded in that count upon which relief may be granted.
8063: Barrett's derivative regulatory takings claim fails as a matter of law because the Enterprises lacked a cognizable property interest in the right to exclude
Without this right to exclude, the Enterprises lack any cognizable property interest on which Barrett may base a derivative Fifth Amendment takings claim.
8084: Takings: seizure of cash and property during a criminal investigation is not a taking under the Fifth Amendment, so the takings claim fails.
when property has been seized pursuant to the criminal laws . . . , such deprivations are not 'takings' for which the owner is entitled to compensation.
8104: Takings: whether the DOJ Bump-Stock-Type Devices Final Rule requiring destruction or surrender of bump stocks effected a compensable taking; court held plaintiffs lacked a protectable property interest in continued possession or transferability.
plaintiffs lacked a property right in what they allege was taken—continued possession or transferability of their bump-stock-type devices.
8256: Takings: the complaint failed to state a physical takings claim. Government failure to install pumps or build a floodway is not a taking, the Mississippi levee theory was not pleaded, and the Backwater Project theory did not plausibly allege but-for worse flooding.
The government's failure to install pumps or to construct an additional floodway cannot result in takings liability.
8408: Takings: whether the amended complaint plausibly alleged a taking by the United States through affirmative government action (flowage easement from flooding caused by the Cherokee Nation's development after the government took land into trust); held no taking claim stated.

Therefore, Ms. Berry has not stated a viable takings claim against the government based on the United States' decision to acquire in trust the Cherokee Spring Site and allow the Nation's construction plans on the site.
8433: Takings claim based on alleged taking of plaintiff's Ethiopian employment contract through U.S. consular officer's conduct; court held no taking because no facts showed the government assumed the contract for public use.
Mr. Yifru alleges no facts to support that the conduct of a U.S. government official led the United States to assume his employment contract for public purposes.
8575: Takings claim based on lawful tax collection, dismissed as insubstantial because the claimant did not concede the validity of the government action
we do not see error in the Claims Court's finding that the lawful exercise of the government's tax collection powers is not a taking.
8697: Takings: whether the government's actions caused a compensable taking of Chrysler franchise agreements; court held dealers failed to prove the but-for-world loss in value, so no taking shown. Court did not reach the no-coercion ruling.
There is no compensable taking when the alleged economic impact of the government action has not resulted in a diminution in value.
8763: Takings: ROW Agreements (granting clause 'right of way') held to convey easements, not fee simple, so the railroad's interest was limited and the claimants' fee interest in the parcels was not defeated; grants of government summary judgment reversed.

Because we conclude that the Court of Federal Claims erred in finding that the ROW Agreements conveyed fee simple estates rather than easements, we reverse the grants of the government's motions for partial summary judgment as to the relevant parcels
8764: Takings: Purpose Agreements ('for railroad purposes' in granting clause) held to convey easements rather than fee simple; government summary judgment reversed.

Because we conclude that the Court of Federal Claims erred in finding the Purpose Agreements conveyed fee simple estates rather than easements, we reverse the grants of the government's motions for partial summary judgment as to the relevant parcels
8765: Takings: non-instrument parcels (lost conveyance instruments, government failed to prove contents by clear and convincing evidence; claimants established fee interests via centerline presumption) — cognizable property interest found; government summary judgment reversed.

Therefore, we reverse the decision of the Court of Federal Claims granting the government's motion for partial summary judgment as to the non-instrument parcels and denying the Appellants' motion for partial summary judgment as to the same parcels.
9114: Takings Clause claim rejected: foreclosure sale by a private bank under contractual mortgage provisions does not implicate the Takings Clause.
This does not implicate the Takings Clause.
9130: Rails-to-trails takings claim: court affirmed summary judgment that plaintiffs held no compensable property interest because LOTCHR was at least a de facto corporation and took fee simple title by the Shuford deed, so no taking occurred.
we affirm the Claims Court's grant of summary judgment on the basis that LOTCHR was at least a de facto corporation under Florida law at the time of the Shuford deed.
9210: Whether the Final Rule effects a Fifth Amendment taking of previously excluded devices, held no taking because owners lacked a cognizable property interest under McCutchen
we conclude that the district court properly granted summary judgment as to Mr. Doe's takings claim.
9311: Fifth Amendment takings claim based on alleged theft of intellectual property: complaint too conclusory to state a takings claim.
Dr. Aljindi's one-sentence factual allegation regarding his intellectual property theft is too conclusory to support a Fifth Amendment takings claim.
9661: Takings claim under the Fifth Amendment arising from the ATF Bump-Stock-Type Devices Final Rule; Court of Federal Claims dismissed the amended complaint and the Federal Circuit affirmed, so no taking was found.
For the same reasons we today affirm the Claims Court's judgment in the McCutchen case, we affirm the Claims Court's judgment in the present case.
9674: Whether a Fifth Amendment physical or regulatory taking occurred from the conservatorships; court held no cognizable property interest and dismissed the takings claim.
shareholders lack a cognizable property interest in the context of a takings claim.
9700: Takings: the complaint failed to plausibly allege a physical takings claim because it did not show flooding greater than would have occurred without the Backwater Project; government inaction (failure to build pumps) cannot support takings liability.
The Amended Complaint on its face does not plausibly allege any flooding of the Board’s land greater than would have taken place if the Backwater Project had not been built.
9902: Takings claim over DEA-seized vehicles: the court held the police power does not bar takings liability for retaining seized property after the criminal interest ends, vacated summary judgment for the government, and remanded for factual development on the remaining government actions.
there is no police power exception that insulates the United States from takings liability for the period after seized property is no longer needed for criminal proceedings.
10067: Takings: whether the NITU and interim trail use under the easement constituted a compensable taking, based on the court's holding that railbanking and interim trail use fall within the scope of the unrestricted easement, so Stimson had no compensable property interest.
We find that the purpose of the deed here is clear from its express terms and plainly covers unrestricted reasonable use.
10068: Takings: whether the railroad abandoned the easement before the NITU, so that no taking occurred; court held Stimson failed to show abandonment by clear and convincing evidence.
We agree with the Claims Court that Stimson has not met its burden to show by clear and convincing evidence that the Railroad abandoned the easement.
10143: Takings: no cognizable property interest in LLP licenses and A80 QS permits, so the Coast Guard Act sideboards effected no taking of compensable property.
We therefore agree with the Claims Court that FFI did not possess any cognizable property interests in its LLP licenses and A80 QS permits.
10144: Takings: no cognizable property interest in using the vessels to harvest and process fish in the Management Areas.
FFI does not have a compensable property interest in using its vessels to harvest and process fish in the Management Areas.
10209: Takings: whether downstream property owners have a cognizable property interest in flowage easements from flood-control dam releases (Hurricane Harvey); Court of Federal Claims found no cognizable interest, reversed.

We hold that Appellants have alleged cognizable property interests in flowage easements, reverse the decision of the Court of Federal Claims, and remand for further proceedings consistent with this opinion.
10669: Takings: the court held that the NITU effected a temporary physical taking of the landowners' property under the Trails Act, including the causation finding that the railroad would have abandoned the line absent the NITU.
we agree with the Court of Federal Claims that Appellants' property was temporarily taken under the Trails Act.
10670: Takings: duration of the temporary taking; the court held the taking ended on November 8, 2013, when the NITU expired, rather than on January 7, 2014, so the compensation period is shorter.
We agree with the government that the taking ended upon expiration of the NITU on November 8, 2013.
10684: Takings: whether the NITU issuance under the Trails Act took the landowners' property by placing interim trail use outside the scope of the railroad easements. Court held trail use is not a railroad purpose under Missouri law, so the scope was exceeded and a taking occurred.
In sum, the easements granted to the railroad were not broad enough to encompass interim trail use or railbanking, and thus Fifth Amendment takings have occurred.
10685: Takings: whether railbanking (preserving the corridor for possible future rail use) falls within the scope of the railroad easements. Court held it does not, so the railbanking NITU was also a taking.
The mere preservation of a tract of land for possible future rail use under Boyles is not a railroad purpose.
10770: Rails-to-trails takings claim: the court held the Falkner, Brown and George deeds conveyed fee simple interests, so the railbanking authorized by the STB caused no taking; summary judgment for the government affirmed.
We hold that the granting clauses of the subject deeds unambiguously conveyed fee simple interests in the land and not easements despite contradictory language elsewhere in the deeds.
10985: Takings claim dismissed because plaintiff failed to concede validity of the government action (publication of patent application) and identified no compensable taking.
we agree with the trial court that it lacked jurisdiction to hear this claim.
11122: Judicial takings theory: whether an adverse federal district court judgment in a tort case constitutes a taking of plaintiff's cause of action; court held no taking.
a court does not "take" a party's chose in action by ruling against that party on the merits.
11171: Takings framework: permanent but intermittent recurring flooding caused by government action is a per se physical taking, not subject to the Arkansas Game & Fish II multi-factor test; taking found.
We also clarify that permanent recurring floodings are per se takings.
11172: Causation baseline: court held the 2004 Changes were measured against the pre-2004 world under the Hardwicke/Miller exception, not the pre-Mainstem System baseline urged by the Government; St. Bernard Parish held inapplicable.
Plaintiffs are correct that the Hardwicke exception applies and that the Court of Federal Claims did not clearly err in applying it to this case.
11173: Relative benefits defense: court rejected the Government's argument that benefits of the 1944 FCA Mainstem System offset the harm of the 2004 Changes, and affirmed denial of leave to add the defense.
We see no error in the trial court’s application of the relative benefits doctrine.
11175: 2011 flooding causation: trial court clearly erred in finding the Corps' 2011 releases did not cause flood damage; vacated and remanded for further factfinding, without deciding causation on the merits.
Because the trial court clearly erred in both findings, we vacate and remand for further factfinding.
11354: Takings: Building 2001 is not a cognizable Fifth Amendment property interest because it is federal property and the Oahe Act does not recognize tribal ownership.
we agree with the Claims Court that Building 2001 is not a cognizable property interest
11355: Takings: no taking of the Tribal Addition or the trust land beneath the Building, since the government did not physically or regulatorily take them.
we see no basis to disturb the court's determination that the Tribe failed to show a taking
11590: Takings: the court held the 1853 releases conveyed fee simple title under Indiana law, so plaintiffs had no property interest and no compensable taking of the rail corridor occurred.
In sum, we conclude that, under Indiana law, the Releases here conveyed fee simple titles.
11663: Takings: whether mandatory Transitional Reinsurance Program contributions paid from trust accounts were a taking of a cognizable property interest; held they were a mere obligation to pay money, so no taking.
Here, we agree with the Claims Court that, under our precedent, this case involves the mere obligation to pay money.
11671: Takings, rails-to-trails just compensation: the before condition. The court held the before condition must account for the OCSR scenic railroad operating on the corridor under POTB's easement, rejecting the argument that the easement was extinguished and the appraiser's 17-foot right-of-way approach.
The Court of Federal Claims properly concluded that the "before" condition must consider Appellants' property burdened by OCSR's operation of its excursion rail operations on the railroad corridor.
11672: Takings, rails-to-trails just compensation: the after condition. The court held claimants did not prove a diminution in market value from the NITU and Trails Act easement, because the trail was improbable at the NITU date and the easement was not exclusive.
On this record, Appellants have not offered evidence that in 2016 the market believed Appellants' property value would be diminished.
11723: Takings: whether plaintiff had a property interest in the rail corridor so as to support a Fifth Amendment taking claim; court held the 1872 deed unambiguously conveyed fee simple, so no taking claim.

Because the New York and Boston Railroad, and thus its successor-in-interest CSX, held the rail corridor in fee simple, 233rd Street Partnership has no property interest in the rail corridor on which to rest a claim for a taking.
11754: Takings: court held the complaint contained no takings claim and that the plaintiff identified no cognizable property interest supporting a nonfrivolous takings claim, including as to the alleged takings of his claim adjudication, filings, and appellate time.
Mr. Pollitt fails to identify any such interest to support a non-frivolous takings claim—both in his complaint and on appeal.
11866: Physical takings: whether MPRA's modification of pensioners' contract rights under the multiemployer plan was a physical taking; court held no physical taking and that the Claims Court did not err in declining to apply the physical takings analysis.
Thus, the Claims Court did not err in declining to apply the physical takings analysis to plaintiffs’ claims.
11867: Regulatory takings: whether the MPRA benefit reductions were a regulatory taking under the Penn Central factors (economic impact, investment-backed expectations, character of action); court held no regulatory taking.
Under these circumstances, we conclude that the three Penn Central factors weigh in favor of the government, and that there was no regulatory taking.
11890: Physical takings: whether the complaint stated a physical taking based on the CDC eviction moratorium (Cedar Point vs. Yee).
Because we conclude that the complaint stated a claim for a physical taking, we reverse and remand for further proceedings.
11891: Authorization for takings-claim purposes: whether the CDC eviction moratorium, though possibly unlawful, was authorized so as to support takings liability.
We conclude that the Order was "authorized" for takings-claim purposes.
12174: Takings claim dismissed: the complaint did not allege facts establishing a legally cognizable Fifth Amendment property interest in the seized funds.
we agree with the trial court that Ms. Rhee has failed to demonstrate that she has a legally cognizable property interest in the funds seized by the government.
12241: Whether a Fifth Amendment takings claim based on alleged patent infringement by the government is within Court of Federal Claims jurisdiction; held unavailable, § 1498 is the only avenue.
"a cause of action under the Fifth Amendment is unavailable to patent owners alleging infringement by the government."
12378: Takings: the court held that plaintiffs failed to show the NITU caused a temporary taking under Caquelin, because the railroad would not have abandoned absent the NITU, so no compensable taking was established.
On this record, we cannot say that the Claims Court erred in determining that Sauer failed to adduce sufficient evidence to support causation.
12379: Takings: state-law abandonment is irrelevant because the easement was limited to railroad use, so it cannot supply an alternative path to a taking.

It is thus irrelevant whether as a matter of state law Great Western could have abandoned the Line, since under federal law, it would have had to seek permission from the STB to consummate abandonment in any case.
13065: Takings claim fails because a statutory right to be paid money is not a property interest for Takings Clause purposes; no taking found.
Mr. Hamilton has not stated a Takings Claim within the Claims Court's jurisdiction
13230: Takings liability: cognizable property interest in flowage easements, permanent or temporary flooding taking, and rejection of police power, Flood Control Act and necessity defenses; liability decision affirmed.
Having held that Plaintiffs had a property interest, that a taking occurred, and that no defense applies, we affirm the Liability Decision.
13238: Takings: whether oyster lessees had a cognizable property interest, so that the 2019 Spillway operation did not effect a compensable permanent taking; court held the 2006 Louisiana statutes subordinated the leases and barred the claim, so no taking claim.
Because Appellants failed to demonstrate the existence of a cognizable property interest for Fifth Amendment purposes, our "task is at an end."
13434: Physical versus regulatory taking: the court held United's alleged taking of water rights through NMFS's ESA bypass-flow requirements is regulatory, not physical, so no physical taking was pleaded.
United's complaint therefore alleges a taking that is regulatory in nature.
13637: Takings: regulatory takings claim held unripe because no final decision on the Incidental Take Permit application; dismissal affirmed
His takings claim is unripe and the trial court properly dismissed it.
13866: Takings: Whether the rail-to-trails NITUs effected a Fifth Amendment taking of landowners' fee simple title to the Manship and Vanlaningham Parcels, turning on whether the railroad held only an easement (Manship Decree construction, Indiana centerline presumption, lost Vanlaningham deed).
Accordingly, we affirm the Court of Federal Claims' judgment for Plaintiffs as to the Manship Parcels.
13954: Fifth Amendment takings claim based on facilities and lost helium volumes dismissed for failure to state a claim; no taking adequately alleged
We therefore affirm the Claims Court's dismissal of Keyes' takings claim.
13955: Takings: whether the NITU issuance effected a Fifth Amendment taking, resolved by holding the deeds and Condemnation Judgment conveyed fee simple so no reversionary interest existed and no taking occurred.
Accordingly, we conclude that each deed conveyed to the railroad an interest in fee simple such that there was no Fifth Amendment taking.
14262: Takings: whether the government's enactment of PROMESA, through the Oversight Board's restructuring of COFINA bonds, constituted a taking; court held no taking because the government lacked coercive control over the Board.
the United States lacks the requisite amount of coercive control over the Oversight Board’s actions to create liability under the Fifth Amendment.
14346: Takings claim based on government use of plaintiff's research: dismissed as time-barred under 28 U.S.C. §2501 for the NSTC publication, precluded by res judicata as to the other uses, and not facially plausible as to a cognizable property interest.
Regarding the takings claim related to a published strategic plan of the NSTC, the Claims Court properly held that claim to be time-barred by 28 U.S.C. § 2501.
14413: Takings: constructive taking theory based on government inaction and deprivation caused by Per Scholas rather than any government action.
But government inaction cannot support a takings claim.
14434: Takings: the court held Horton failed to allege a nonfrivolous takings claim because the alleged employee conduct was unauthorized, so no compensable taking was shown.
The Court of Federal Claims did not err in determining that Mr. Horton failed to allege a nonfrivolous takings claim.
14494: Whether Ligado has a property interest protected by the Takings Clause against non-FCC agency actions; the court did not decide it and vacated the Claims Court's ruling that a property right was pleaded, remanding for further analysis.
We vacate the Claims Court's decision insofar as it holds that Ligado has pleaded the existence of a property right and that DoD use of the spectrum might qualify as a physical taking.
14495: Whether DoD's use of the spectrum could qualify as a physical taking; the court did not decide the categorization issue and vacated the Claims Court's ruling on it, remanding.
We do not decide the physical-taking issue raised by the government in challenging the Claims Court's refusal to dismiss Ligado's physical-taking claim.
14673: Midview Exchange takings claim (claim 10): inadequate bargained-for consideration cannot support a taking, and Non-Intercourse Act violations cannot ground a takings claim; dismissal affirmed.
Accordingly, we affirm the Claims Court's dismissal of claim 10.
14778: Takings claim based on alleged taking of children and family; court held no property right in children, so no taking.
There is no case law or statute which establishes a property right in children.
14949: Takings: whether a retention bonus expectation and reassignment of medical services labor constitute a cognizable Fifth Amendment property interest taken without compensation; held not cognizable, dismissal affirmed.

We agree with the Claims Court that both Dr. Mathai's expectation of a retention bonus from VA and his expectation of not being assigned particular duties associated with the organizational-chart change for the Pain Management Section are not cognizable property interests protected by the Fifth Amendment.
14961: Fifth Amendment takings claim over the IRS sale of the property: dismissal affirmed because Noll did not concede the validity of the government action and the record did not support a taking claim.
Again, there is nothing in the record to support a finding that Mr. Noll has conceded the validity of the government's sale of his property.
15032: Takings: no compensable property interest in Reclamation-delivered water under California law, so the takings claims fail.
Therefore, we affirm the Court of Federal Claims' dismissal of these claims.
15231: Takings: the court held the claimant's asserted property interests (right to international travel and passport) are not cognizable property interests, so no taking is shown.
Neither meets a legally cognizable property interest for a taking.
15245: Takings claim based on clerk's office docketing of plaintiff's filing dismissed; no taking found because the document was not appropriated for public use and the claim sounded in tort.
Although a document was publicly filed on a court docket, it does not mean it was taken for public use within the meaning of the Fifth Amendment
